## Finally, Freedom from Your CPAP Mask

If you're struggling with CPAP—can't sleep with the mask, tired of the noise, or frustrated with
poor results—you're not alone.** Over 15 million Americans have tried and failed with CPAP
therapy.**

### What is Inspire Therapy?

Inspire is the only FDA-approved implantable treatment for obstructive sleep apnea. It works from
inside your body to deliver mild stimulation to key airway muscles, keeping your airway open during
sleep.
* **No mask, no hose, no machine** – Just sleep naturally
* **Works with your natural breathing** – Gentle stimulation only when needed
* **Simple remote control** – Turn on before bed, off when you wake

### Proven Results That Matter

of patients say Inspire is better than CPAP
Based on 5-year STAR trial follow-up data
79%
reduction in sleep apnea events

partners report quiet sleep

*Individual results may vary. Clinical outcomes based on properly selected candidates who meet

Join 2,400+ patients this month who discovered freedom from CPAP • Complete in under 3 minutes

## Why Patients Choose Inspire Over CPAP

We understand your CPAP frustrations. Here's how Inspire is different and why it might be the
solution you've been searching for.

### CPAP Challenges
* Mask discomfort and claustrophobia
* Hose tangles and air leaks
* Machine noise disrupting sleep
* Travel complications and bulky equipment
* Dry mouth and skin irritation
* Partner disturbance and intimacy issues

### Inspire Freedom
* Sleep naturally without a mask
* No equipment, hoses, or maintenance
* Silent operation for you and your partner
* Travel freely – no packing equipment
* Natural sleep position and movement
* Intimacy and relationship benefits

## Could Inspire Be Right for You?

Inspire therapy is specifically designed for people with moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnea
who cannot use or benefit from CPAP therapy.

### You may be a candidate if you:

Have moderate to severe sleep apnea (AHI 15-65)
Cannot tolerate or benefit from CPAP
Are 18 years or older
Have a BMI of 35 or less
Do not have complete concentric collapse at the soft palate
Are willing to use the device every night
**Important:** Only a qualified sleep specialist can determine if Inspire therapy is right for you.
Candidacy requires a comprehensive evaluation including sleep study results, medical history review,
and drug-induced sleep endoscopy (DISE) procedure.

### Important Safety Information

#### Inspire therapy is not recommended for patients with:
* •Cardiac pacemakers or other implanted electrical devices that may interfere with the Inspire
  system
* •Inability to operate the Inspire remote control or understand device instructions
* •Pregnancy (safety during pregnancy has not been established)
* •Active infection at the potential implant site
* •Central or mixed sleep apnea comprising more than 25% of total sleep apnea events
* •Complete concentric collapse of the soft palate (determined via drug-induced sleep endoscopy)

#### Risks and Considerations:
* •Surgical risks including bleeding, infection, pain, and potential nerve injury
* •Device malfunction may require additional surgery for replacement
* •Battery replacement required every 9-11 years through outpatient surgery

Individual results may vary. Efficacy data based on the STAR clinical trial (N=126 patients) with
specific inclusion criteria. Discuss all risks and benefits with your qualified sleep medicine
physician.

Take our quick assessment to determine your candidacy and connect with qualified providers near you.

If you're struggling with CPAP—can't sleep with the mask, tired of the noise, or frustrated with
poor results—you're not alone.** Over 15 million Americans have tried and failed with CPAP
therapy.**

### What is Inspire Therapy?

Inspire is the only FDA-approved implantable treatment for obstructive sleep apnea. It works from
inside your body to deliver mild stimulation to key airway muscles, keeping your airway open during
sleep.
* **No mask, no hose, no machine** – Just sleep naturally
* **Works with your natural breathing** – Gentle stimulation only when needed
* **Simple remote control** – Turn on before bed, off when you wake

We understand your CPAP frustrations. Here's how Inspire is different and why it might be the
solution you've been searching for.

### CPAP Challenges
* Mask discomfort and claustrophobia
* Hose tangles and air leaks
* Machine noise disrupting sleep
* Travel complications and bulky equipment

* Partner disturbance and intimacy issues

### Inspire Freedom
* Sleep naturally without a mask

* Silent operation for you and your partner

* Intimacy and relationship benefits

## Could Inspire Be Right for You?

Inspire therapy is specifically designed for people with moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnea
who cannot use or benefit from CPAP therapy.

### You may be a candidate if you:

Have moderate to severe sleep apnea (AHI 15-65)
Cannot tolerate or benefit from CPAP
Are 18 years or older
Have a BMI of 35 or less
Do not have complete concentric collapse at the soft palate
Are willing to use the device every night
**Important:** Only a qualified sleep specialist can determine if Inspire therapy is right for you.
Candidacy requires a comprehensive evaluation including sleep study results, medical history review,
and drug-induced sleep endoscopy (DISE) procedure.

  system

While other brands attempt to differentiate themselves by adding features such as tongue straps and
mandible adjustments, SleepTight has focused on delivering a product that fits properly and is
comfortable. This is one of the *most important* features to look for, as a properly fitted
mouthpiece is less likely to fall out at night. Losing a dental guard while asleep happens to be one
of the most common complaints among users.

SleepTight is able to achieve a closer, tighter fit because of its patented dual-laminate design.

mouthpieces. Unlike most Snoring Mouthpiece that are sold, this one is *actually* **made in the

necessity for those who tend to breathe through their mouth during sleep or cannot breathe through
their nose because of a cold or allergies.

  over 40 years in dentistry and is familiar with the application of oral appliances.
* It was [cleared by the FDA ][17]in 2014 as a class II medical device and is described as an
  intraoral device for snoring.

[ Visit site ][12]

Are you looking for *real reviews* on Snoring Mouthpieces but are only finding the same old reviews
that have been rehashed?

Wouldn’t it be nice if someone were to actually test several mouthpieces and then write an *honest
comprehensive* review of each? Over the years, I’ve been doing just that.

It all started with a journey to stop my own snoring which led me to create this blog and ultimately
review more than 30 different mouthguards.

First things first, if you don’t already know what a snoring mouthpiece is, the [information
below][13] should answer most of your questions. In short, it’s an oral appliance similar to an
athletic guard or dental guard but is designed to hold the jaw or tongue forward which tightens the
airway and stops snoring.

Do they work? *Without a doubt*.

Now that I have mentioned my top 3 choices, here’s a bit more information summarizing why each
mouthpiece was chosen.

## **SleepTight #1**


☆☆☆☆☆ 5.00 Star

[Read SleepTight Review][14]

While SleepTight is a brand that you may not have heard of, it’s simple and incredibly effective.

What makes the SleepTight stand out from the crowd is its simplicity, effectiveness, and value.
While other brands attempt to differentiate themselves by adding features such as tongue straps and
mandible adjustments, SleepTight has focused on delivering a product that fits properly and is
comfortable. This is one of the *most important* features to look for, as a properly fitted
mouthpiece is less likely to fall out at night. Losing a dental guard while asleep happens to be one
of the most common complaints among users.

SleepTight is able to achieve a closer, tighter fit because of its patented dual-laminate design. 
The outer trays are made from a stiff FDA approved thermoplastic material while the inner core is a
soft material that creates a better impression of the teeth as compared to other snoring
mouthpieces. Unlike most Snoring Mouthpiece that are sold, this one is *actually* **made in the
United States.**

There is one large front breathing hole, the largest opening that I have come across. This is a
necessity for those who tend to breathe through their mouth during sleep or cannot breathe through
their nose because of a cold or allergies.

Another reason why I have rated this product highly is that it’s a great value. The manufacturer of
Sleeptight has offered the readers of this blog a **BOGO deal**, which can not be found elsewhere.
In order to receive this offer, you must visit [this page][15] on the company’s website.

Also, SleepTight offers a 30-Day Trial for just $9.95. You are charged only $9.95 and can try the
SleepTight to ensure you are satisfied before the balance is charged.

Here are a few other reasons why SleepTight has earned a spot in second place:
* Made in the United States
* Designed by Dr. Michael Williams, member of the [American Academy of Sleep Medicine][16] who spent
  over 40 years in dentistry and is familiar with the application of oral appliances.
* It was [cleared by the FDA ][17]in 2014 as a class II medical device and is described as an
  intraoral device for snoring.
* SleepTight is extremely durable, lasting up to 24 months. Most mouthguards only last between 6-12
  months.

## **Good Morning Snore Solution #2**


☆☆☆☆☆ 4.75 Star

[Read GMSS Review][18]

Tried and true, the Good Morning Snore Solution (GMSS) has long been a favorite of mine and a
popular choice among snorers.

It’s a Tongue Stabilizing Device (TSD) style mouthpiece that’s similar in design to other TSD’s,
although it sports a lower profile that is notably more compact in comparison. Also, the material
that the GMSS uses is slightly thinner in nature in comparison to other TSD’s. Being a TSD, it
*does* require that your nasal passages be free of obstruction in order to allow for proper
breathing while asleep. If you are a mouth breather, you will *not* want to use this product.

The GMSS is a one-size-fits-all mouthguard that requires no alterations before being used.  It’s BPA
free, latex free, and is made from a medical grade silicone.

Denture wearers are often limited in terms of mouthpiece choices. The GMSS is one of few products
that’s suitable for snorers who wear dentures.

While it’s one of the better products out there, it does come at a higher than average price tag.

**Save 10% on your order using Promo Code: SMGSAVE10**

Visit the [GMSS website][19] for more information.

Other key points that helped GMSS earn a third-place finish are:
* It was developed by Dr. Leslie Dort, a Canadian dentist in Calgary, Canada.
* In [this study][20], GMSS was found to significantly reduce snoring.  Very few mouthguards have
  been studied in a clinical setting.
* GMSS is Cleared by the [FDA][21], ARTG, and EC.
* You can try it risk-free for 30 days. If not satisfied, It can be returned for a full refund.

## **SnoreRx #3**


☆☆☆☆☆ 4.50 Star

[Read SnoreRx Review][22]

SnoreRx  is a pioneer in the industry and is a trusted source when it comes to snoring mouthpieces.
The company was one of the first to enter the industry in 2009 when it offered its unique Thermal
Matrix and Micro-Fit features. I have been a fan of this product since I first gave it a try in
2013.

They offer two different designs which include the Original SnoreRx and the SnoreRx Plus with the
primary difference being the SnoreRx Plus allows for vertical movement of your jaw. Both products
can be micro-adjusted at any time in 1-millimeter increments as needed without the use of any
special tools. Their products are laboratory-quality and are top-notch. 

If you have read any of my reviews, you know how much I love mouthpieces that allow for mouth
breathing. The SnoreRx delivers in this category as well with a very large breather hole located at
the front of the device. 

Here are a few other reasons why SnoreRx has earned a spot at the top:
* Laboratory-quality mouthpiece at an affordable price.
* Ability to make micro-adjustments without the need for special tools.
* [Cleared by the FDA ][23]in 2011 as a class II medical device and is BPA Free
* Endorsed by several medical professionals.
* Comes with a 30-day money-back guarantee.

# Offering a unique delivery model to treating obstructive sleep apnea.

Clark O. Taylor B.A., D.D.S., M.D.

[ Learn More About Our Delivery Model ][49]
[Dr. Clark O. Taylor]

## Let us help you find a solution.

Do you snore? Wake up gasping for air?

You deserve a quality nights sleep. Take a few minutes to fill out our simple sleep apnea
questionnaire to see if you are at high or low risk of suffering from obstructive sleep apnea.

[ Find The Right Solution. Start Here. ][50]

## Watch our free webinar

Is sleep apnea surgery right for you?

Patient education is the most important step toward combating obstructive sleep apnea. Learn more
about your options including OSA surgery and our unique delivery model.

[ Watch Our Free Webinar Now ][51]

## Schedule a consultation

Ready to take the next step?

Our team is ready to discuss your options and create a personalized treatment plan. Take control of
your sleep health today.

[ Schedule a Consult Today ][52]

## Our Unique OSA Treatment Model

Founded on the well-documented success of bimaxillary advancement surgery for sleep apnea (also
known as maxillomandibular advancement), Surgical Sleep Solutions has developed a unique obstructive
sleep apnea treatment model for delivery that eliminates the majority of negatives commonly
associated with this procedure. Our model, which has a **success rate of 95 to 99 percent**, has not
been duplicated.

Dr. Clark O. Taylor has extensive training and experience in maxillofacial surgery and has performed
hundreds of bimaxillary advancement surgeries. His unique approach combines the latest surgical
techniques with comprehensive patient care to achieve outstanding results.

If you or someone you know suffers from obstructive sleep apnea and has been unable to tolerate CPAP
therapy, bimaxillary advancement surgery may be the solution you've been looking for.

[ Learn More About Our Treatment Model ][53]

## Understanding Obstructive Sleep Apnea

Let us help you understand your sleep disorder and your various treatment options.

[ Watch Our Sleep Apnea Webinar Now ][54]
[Sleep apnea surgery at Surgical Sleep Solutions]

## Ready to Get Started?

Take the first step toward better sleep and better health. Schedule your consultation today.
